summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the descriptions of paradise, focusing on a hadith narration about the lowest and highest ranking people in paradise. He begins by explaining the story of Muriel bin Sha, a former desert bandit who accepted Islam, became an excellent Muslim, and was among the Prophet's guards at the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Sh. Ali Mashhour then presents the main hadith where the Prophet Muhammad is asked about the description of the lowest-ranking person in paradise—the last person to enter after being punished in hellfire. This person will be granted fifty times the dominion of the greatest earthly kings, plus everything his soul desires and his eyes seek in pleasure. In contrast, Sh. Ali Mashhour explains that the highest people in paradise have been prepared by Allah Himself with His own hand, with rewards that no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined. He concludes by noting a related hadith about three things Allah created with His own hand: Prophet Adam, the Torah given to Moses, and the trees of paradise.
suggested_title: The Descriptions of Paradise: From the Lowest to the Highest Ranks
catchy_title: What awaits the last person to enter paradise?
